set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: staff report for Legistar 25-1513, Resolution 143-2025 and the revised August 2025 plan match the $2,990,478 five-year estimate, year 1-3 amounts, the 2024 single-activity capital amendment and the 2025 shift to navigation center operations; HCD 2024-2028 NOFA confirms $308,950, $318,390 and $1,930,938. prevailing_wage_trigger true has no basis cited, and neither the 2019 nor the 2024-2028 PLHA guidelines or NOFA mention prevailing wage; the funds go to operations, so this should likely be unclear pending a Tier 3 review.

reason: Award figures, uses and closed status match the staff report, resolution, plan and HCD NOFA.

set.per_unit_cap: No cap for projects that receive LIHTC or are financed with tax-exempt bonds or local, state or federal loans or grants (R&T 214(g)(1)(A)-(B)). The $20 million assessed-value cap per taxpayer applies only to exemptions claimed solely under the 90 percent lower income occupancy rule (R&T 214(g)(1)(C)).
set.next_deadline: File BOE-267 (first year) or BOE-267-A (annual) with the Assessor by February 15 each year. Late claims filed by January 1 of the next year can cancel 90 percent of tax, penalty and interest, and later claims 85 percent, with the combined tax, penalty and interest capped at $250. Property acquired after the January 1 lien date must file within 90 days of the first of the month after acquisition or by February 15 of the following year, whichever is earlier. Supplemental forms BOE-267-L or BOE-267-L1 attach as applicable.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: source_url only confirms the Assessor contact (Jon DeVille, 530-621-5719); substantive rules checked against BOE Publication 149 and R&T 214. The $20 million cap was misattributed to all non-LIHTC regulatory-agreement projects; it applies only to the 90 percent occupancy route, not to government-financed projects. 80 percent AMI (lower income per HSC 50079.5) is correct. prevailing_wage_trigger false is uncited; it is a property tax exemption, not construction funding.

reason: Material: per_unit_cap misstated the $20 million cap as applying to government-financed non-LIHTC projects, and next_deadline late-filing terms corrected to the BOE rule.
